findings.title: AI analysis reports shown to buyers are always synthetic fixture data, dated as current, labelled reconciled, with no demo marker
evidence: rg over reports/templates and render.py for synthetic|fixture|demo => exit 1

findings.title: Default PAID_MEDIA_DATA_MODE=auto mixes synthetic Google/Meta/Reddit tools into a live catalog when only direct adapters are configured
findings.description: With no Pipeboard token and X/OpenAI keys present, mode auto builds catalog source 'fixture+direct' with CompositeReadProvider(FixtureReadProvider(), direct_providers); compare_periods would total fixture rows with live X spend (same USD, same windows) and report reconciled. Unreachable through docker-compose because serve_demo refuses non-sample, hence P2 here; P1 for any direct `paid-media-agent serve` deployment.
findings.recommendation: Never mix: default to live-or-sample, or flag fixture-sourced rows and suppress totals that mix fixture:// with direct/pipeboard sources.

findings.title: Overview ROAS tile is always 0x and spend tile sums across currencies and providers; undefined metrics render as 0
findings.description: readReport requests spend/impressions/clicks/conversions/roas but live-data computes headline ROAS from conversion_value, which is therefore always 0 -> '0x' whenever spend > 0. The same block sums spend across all rows regardless of row.currency/provider. formatNumber renders undefined as 0, so untracked per-row ROAS/conversions print as 0.
findings.recommendation: Use the report tool's summary.groups (currency-grouped, spend-weighted ROAS) or request conversion_value; group tiles by currency; render null/undefined as a dash.

findings.title: Platform providers (and sandbox) emit 0 for undefined ratios, contradicting the 'missing is never zero' rule
findings.description: cpa = conversions>0 ? spend/conversions : 0, roas = spend>0 ? value/spend : 0, etc. A campaign with spend and no tracked conversions shows CPA 0 and ROAS 0; Meta counts only omni_purchase so lead-gen accounts always show conversions 0. summarizeReport is careful but only sees what providers emit.
findings.recommendation: Emit undefined for zero-denominator ratios and untracked conversion metrics; render as dash.

findings.title: Clicks and conversions summed across platforms with different definitions and attribution; ATTRIBUTION_DIFFERS never raised
findings.description: Engine prefers Meta all-clicks over link_clicks and accepts objective-dependent 'results' as conversions; attribution metadata is stored but never compared; cross-platform totals derive CVR/CPA/ROAS from summed conversions across 7d-click, 28-day swipe, click+view purchases and objective results. Engine X uses clicks while adport X uses url_clicks. Only the rendered report carries a one-line caveat; the model-facing summary, dashboard and report-tool summary do not.
findings.recommendation: Carry attribution and click_definition on rows; raise ATTRIBUTION_DIFFERS and suppress or caveat cross-platform ratio metrics while keeping spend totals.

findings.title: Live reads have no provider-reported currency, timezone or completeness; labels come from static TOML and partial days count as complete
evidence: probe 6 (today's row is_complete True) and probe 10 (SAR row labelled USD)
findings.description: PipeboardReadProvider and the direct adapters return payload only; reads.py falls back to the accounts TOML currency/timezone and data_complete_through=None, so every live row is complete and today's partial spend compares against full days as a drop; a row-level account_currency is never checked, so the currency printed next to every figure is operator-typed.
findings.recommendation: Require provider currency/timezone (X and OpenAI already fetch them), flag disagreement with the binding, and derive data_complete_through from a per-platform lag table at minimum.

findings.title: compare_periods double-counts duplicate sources and accepts overlapping windows
evidence: probe 1: 70.00 USD platform, 140.00 USD total, reconciled True
findings.description: No uniqueness check on (platform, account_ref) across artifact_ids chosen by the model; a campaign-grain and ad-group-grain read, or a retried read, doubles the cross-platform total while still labelled reconciled. Overlapping current/previous windows pass validation.
findings.recommendation: Dedupe by (platform, account_ref), reject overlapping windows, add a cross-artifact reconciliation check for the same account.

findings.title: INCOMPLETE_WINDOW is over-sensitive to sparse entities and has no live signal
evidence: probe 3: one campaign with rows on even days only => platform incomplete_window, total suppressed
findings.description: Any entity with fewer rows than days (paused campaign, provider omitting zero-activity days) marks the platform window incomplete and suppresses the cross-platform total; meanwhile live reads have no completeness signal (J6-06). The flag cannot be trusted in either direction.
findings.recommendation: Derive platform completeness from provider freshness, not entity coverage; report sparse entities separately.

findings.title: Day assignment and time-zone handling make daily rows non-comparable across sources
evidence: probe 4 (mixed tz total produced, no flag)
findings.description: Multi-day Meta rows are booked on date_start; engine X assigns days at UTC midnight but labels rows with the account timezone; adport Reddit queries UTC while Google/Meta use account-local dates and Snap/X compute account midnight; cross-platform totals ignore timezone differences.
findings.recommendation: Carry the reporting timezone per row, honour date_stop, raise TIMEZONE_MISMATCH when combining.

findings.title: 'reconciled' is a near-tautology in live mode but surfaced to the buyer as assurance

key_findings: P1: in this repo's deployment the engine can only read synthetic fixtures (compose pins sample; serve_demo asserts sample in both engine modes), yet the Reports page shows those fabricated spend/CPA figures with current dates and a 'reconciled' badge under 'AI analysis reports' with no demo label even when MARKTING_DEMO_MODE=false; README claims analysis of connected accounts.

Engine arithmetic is sound (ratio-of-sums, Decimal, missing-not-zero) but its safety rails are weaker than they look: compare_periods double-counts duplicate artifacts (test codifies it), accepts overlapping windows, never raises attribution/timezone/currency flags, and 'reconciled' is a tautology outside fixtures.

Live engine reads carry no provider currency/timezone/freshness: currency labels come from a static TOML, today's partial day counts as complete, and INCOMPLETE_WINDOW instead over-triggers on sparse entities and suppresses totals.

Platform providers emit 0 for undefined CPA/ROAS/CPC/CTR (contradicting reporting-semantics.md and the report tool's own description); the overview ROAS tile is always 0x because conversion_value is never requested, and spend is summed across currencies without showing currency.

Cross-platform conversions/clicks mix definitions (Meta all-clicks vs link clicks, 'results', omni_purchase, Snap swipes with hard-coded 28-day attribution, TikTok objective 'conversion', Reddit click+view purchases, X clicks vs url_clicks) with no flag anywhere a buyer looks.
Default PAID_MEDIA_DATA_MODE=auto mixes fixture Google/Meta/Reddit tools into a live catalog when only direct adapters exist (mitigated here by serve_demo's sample assertion).
Sandbox synthetic report metrics are formula-generated and unlabelled but currently unreachable from any UI path (bridge calls guarded writes only).
Reddit conversion value unit (/100 vs spend /1e6) and real Pipeboard payload shapes are unverified offline.
